items.title: REST vs gRPC: ek server doosre server ko kaise bulaye
items.one_idea: REST and gRPC are two ways for one server to call another: REST sends readable text over plain HTTP to named resources and works with every tool and browser; gRPC calls a named function from a shared contract file, sends compact binary, and supports streaming; the axis that decides is who is calling (anyone, including browsers and outside partners, versus your own services that you control on both sides).
items.spoken_hook: Servers की बातचीत गलत चुनी, तो पूरा app अटकेगा।

items.hook_10s: Servers की बातचीत गलत चुनी, तो पूरा app अटकेगा। Order करते ही एक server दूसरे server को call करता है, और इसके दो आम तरीके हैं: REST और gRPC। एक सबसे आसान, दूसरा अपनों के बीच तेज़। कब कौन सा? [frame 0: two server boxes with an arrow between them carrying a readable text card on the top arrow and a small dense block of dots on the bottom arrow, an app phone icon above showing a spinner]

hook_candidates.text: Servers की बातचीत गलत चुनी, तो पूरा app अटकेगा।
Interviewer ने पूछा: दो internal services आपस में बात करें, तो REST लोगे या gRPC?
एक server दूसरे server को call कैसे करता है?

items.problem_line: आपका एक app अंदर से कई छोटे servers में बँटा होता है, और वो हर request पर एक-दूसरे को call करते हैं। उस call का तरीका गलत चुना तो या तो बाहर वालों के लिए इस्तेमाल करना मुश्किल, या अंदर वाली हर call ज़रूरत से भारी।
items.visual_idea: Two server boxes, Orders and Payments. Top lane (REST): an arrow labelled with a small request card 'GET /orders/42' travels to Payments and comes back as a readable text card with fields; a phone, a browser and a partner box can all plug into the same arrow. Bottom lane (gRPC): a shared contract sheet sits between both servers, a function-call arrow 'GetOrder(42)' goes across as a compact block of dots, and the answer streams back as a row of small blocks one after another. Last, two boxes 'outside callers' and 'your own services' slide to the matching lane.
items.everyday_anchor: Sending a letter in plain language that anyone at any post office can read (REST), versus two offices that agreed on a fixed printed form and a shorthand code, so their forms are short and quick but nobody else can read them without the form guide (gRPC).
items.example: EXAMPLE (invented): the Orders service needs an order's status from the Payments service. With REST it sends GET /payments/42 and reads a JSON text reply; with gRPC it calls GetPayment(42) from a shared contract file and gets a compact binary reply. No speed numbers are claimed.
facts_to_verify: REST = a group of architecture design constraints; a resource is transferred via standardized client/server interactions; in everyday use a 'REST API' means an HTTP service callable with standard web libraries and tools, and does not always follow every REST constraint (MDN Glossary REST) - fetched. Do not claim REST must use JSON; say 'usually JSON' only as 'commonly', or label it an example.

HTTP methods: GET retrieves a resource representation, POST submits and often changes state, PUT replaces, DELETE deletes (MDN HTTP Methods) - fetched. The page does not define 'idempotent'; if used, define it in one plain sentence or drop it.

gRPC: a client calls a method on a server on another machine as if it were a local object; services are defined in .proto files; protocol buffers are both its interface definition language and its message format; clients and servers can be written in different supported languages; code is generated with protoc and a gRPC plugin; the client has a stub with the same methods (grpc.io introduction) - fetched.

gRPC has four method kinds: unary, server streaming, client streaming, bidirectional streaming; clients can set a deadline (grpc.io core concepts) - fetched. Show at most unary and one streaming kind.

gRPC is carried over HTTP/2 framing (gRPC PROTOCOL-HTTP2.md, fetched). HTTP/2 allows multiple concurrent exchanges on one connection and compresses header fields; binary message framing (RFC 9113 abstract and intro, section 5) - fetched. Say it in one clause; do not teach HTTP/2.

Protocol Buffers: a language-neutral, platform-neutral mechanism for serializing structured data; the page says it is 'like JSON, except smaller and faster'; messages cannot be fully interpreted without the .proto file; new fields can be added without breaking old code (protobuf.dev overview) - fetched. Say 'compact binary, usually smaller than JSON text'; do NOT give any 'N times faster' or size number.

Browsers: gRPC-Web is the route from browsers, and the grpc.io example puts a proxy (Envoy) in between; the page does not say flatly that browsers cannot call gRPC. Say 'browsers typically need gRPC-Web and a proxy'.

Do NOT claim 'gRPC is faster' flatly, nothing about any company using one or the other, no numbers. Axis = who calls (outside, unknown callers vs your own services on both sides) and whether you need streaming.
Define in plain words once: REST, gRPC, contract file (.proto). At most three terms; mention JSON and HTTP/2 only as one-clause asides. Define 'service' as one small server doing one job.
